# Project Management Web Platform

A TypeScript API for projects, tasks, accounts, and session-based access control. It is a clean-room
implementation of a fifth-semester Web Systems Programming specification: 116 real-socket tests run
without a database, and the repository keeps one runtime dependency with no build output to commit.

## Policy before persistence

Authorization lives in pure functions over already-loaded entities in `src/domain/authz.ts`. Use
cases load a resource, make an explicit access decision, then write. The `Actor` type carries only
the authenticated user id and role needed for a policy decision, and the helpers make the difference
between visibility, modification, deletion, and administration explicit.

The policy also handles information boundaries deliberately. A caller who cannot see a resource gets
the response appropriate to that visibility boundary, while an assignee who already knows a task
exists receives a direct denial if they try to delete it. Session authentication re-reads the user
record, so a current role or block status remains authoritative.

## Storage as a port

The service layer depends on the `Store` boundary rather than a database implementation.
`MemoryStore` and `JsonFileStore` share the same repository contract, including normalised email
addresses and task cleanup when a parent project is removed. That makes the HTTP API testable against
real local servers while keeping persistence adapters interchangeable.

Configuration is fail-closed: the service requires its session secret from the environment rather than
using a default. Password hashing uses `node:crypto.scrypt`, tokens use `createHmac`, and Node
runs the typed source directly for development.

## Verification

`npm run check` runs TypeScript checking and 116 tests against a real server and socket. On
2026-08-12 it passed unchanged. `node tools/mutation-check.mjs` copies the tree to a temporary
directory, applies 12 controlled policy mutations one at a time, and confirms that each makes at
least one selected test fail: 12/12 were caught in the local audit.

## Boundaries

The repository concentrates on the server contract. It has no browser front end, no Mongo adapter,
and no multi-process JSON-file adapter. Those are deliberate limits rather than features implied by
the API surface. The published `NOTICE` records the clean-room provenance and course-material
boundary.
